proofs.proof_tex:
Fix \(a\in\{1,2\}\), suppress \(a\) from the notation, and relabel the latent coordinates in the order \(\rho_a\). Write \(X_k=X_{s(a,k)}\) and \(H_{1:k}=(H_{\rho_a(1)},\ldots,H_{\rho_a(k)})\). By Assumption~\textnormal{ass:double-triangular}, every latent parent of \(X_k\) is among \(H_{1:k}\), and \(H_k\) is a parent. Assumption~\textnormal{ass:markov} therefore gives
\[
 P(X_{1:m}=x_{1:m}\mid H=h)
 =\prod_{k=1}^{m}P(X_k=x_k\mid H_{1:k}=h_{1:k})
 =\prod_{k=1}^{m}B_{a,k,h_{1:k-1}}(x_k,h_k).
\]
The first equality uses conditional independence of the observed vertices given all latent vertices; the second uses the absence of later latent parents. In particular, the expression does not depend on \(h_{m+1:K}\).

Let \(M^{(m)}\) be the \(q^m\times q^m\) matrix with the displayed product as its \((x_{1:m},h_{1:m})\) entry. With rows and columns in the induced lexicographic orders, insertion of the intermediate index \((h_{1:m-1},y_m)\) gives, up to the fixed row and column permutations used by the stated conventions,
\[
 M^{(m)}=(M^{(m-1)}\otimes I_q)
 \operatorname{blockdiag}_{u\in\mathcal Q^{m-1}}B_{a,m,u}.
\]
Indeed, the \((x_{1:m},h_{1:m})\) entry of the right-hand side is
\[
 \sum_{u,y_m}M^{(m-1)}(x_{1:m-1},u)
 \mathbf 1\{x_m=y_m\}\mathbf 1\{u=h_{1:m-1}\}
 B_{a,m,u}(y_m,h_m),
\]
which is exactly the preceding product formula. Multiplicativity of the determinant, the block-diagonal determinant formula, and \(\det(C\otimes I_q)=\det(C)^q\) now yield
\[
 \det M^{(m)}=\epsilon_m\det(M^{(m-1)})^q
 \prod_{u\in\mathcal Q^{m-1}}\det(B_{a,m,u}),
\]
where \(\epsilon_m\in\{-1,1\}\) records only the fixed permutations. Starting with \(M^{(1)}=B_{a,1,\varnothing}\) and iterating from \(m=2\) to \(m=K\), a determinant introduced at level \(k\) is raised to the \(q\)-th power once for every later level. Hence
\[
 \det(M_a)=\varepsilon_{q,K}
 \prod_{k=1}^{K}\prod_{u\in\mathcal Q^{k-1}}
 \det(B_{a,k,u})^{q^{K-k}}
 =\varepsilon_{q,K}\Delta_a.
\]
All matrices are finite and square, and no division or limiting argument is used.

For a square \(q^K\times q^K\) matrix, full rank is equivalent to a nonzero determinant. Theorem~\textnormal{thm:local-factorization} and Definition~\textnormal{def:certificate} give
\[
 \det(M_a)\ne0
 \quad\Longleftrightarrow\quad
 \prod_{k=1}^{K}\prod_{u\in\mathcal Q^{k-1}}
 d_{a,k,u}^{q^{K-k}}\ne0
 \quad\Longleftrightarrow\quad
 d_{a,k,u}\ne0\ \text{for every }k,u.
\]
The exponents \(q^{K-k}\) are positive integers. Applying this equivalence for \(a=1,2\) proves
\[
 \Delta_{\mathrm{DT}}\ne0
 \quad\Longleftrightarrow\quad
 \operatorname{rank}(M_1)=\operatorname{rank}(M_2)=q^K.
\]
It also proves directly that \(d_{a,k,u}=0\) forces \(\det(M_a)=0\), hence rank deficiency of view \(a\).

The distinction between column separation and determinant nonvanishing is real already for \(q=3\). Put
\[
 b=\begin{pmatrix}1/3\\1/3\\1/3\end{pmatrix},\qquad
 v=\begin{pmatrix}\delta\\-\delta\\0\end{pmatrix},\qquad
 B=\begin{pmatrix}b-v&b&b+v\end{pmatrix},
 \qquad 0<\delta<1/3.
\]
Every column is a strictly positive probability vector, and the three columns are pairwise distinct. Nevertheless the first plus the third column equals twice the second, so \(\det(B)=0\). Taking this \(B\) as any local conditional table gives the asserted strictly positive ternary boundary witness.

Use the corrected construction in Definition~\textnormal{def:diagonal-dominant-family}. In coordinates consisting of the free entries of the latent and measurement conditional probability tables, every joint cell probability is a polynomial, by Assumption~\textnormal{ass:markov}. Each entry of \(B_{a,k,u}\) is a conditional probability and therefore has the form
\[
 \frac{P(X_{s(a,k)}=x,H_{\rho_a(1:k)}=(u,r))}
 {P(H_{\rho_a(1:k)}=(u,r))}.
\]
Marginalization makes both numerator and denominator polynomial in the table coordinates. Every denominator is strictly positive on \(\Theta_{\Gamma,\Lambda}^{+}\): all latent table entries are positive, so every latent configuration and each of its marginals has positive mass. Determinants and finite products show that \(\Delta_{\mathrm{DT}}\) is rational with a strictly positive common denominator. Denote its polynomial numerator after clearing those denominators by \(N_{\mathrm{DT}}\).

It remains to show that the restriction of this numerator to the affine product of simplices is not the zero polynomial. The corrected family is graph-compatible because its table depends only on \(h_{\operatorname{pa}_{\Gamma}(j)}\); it is Markov by construction and is strictly positive by the stipulated upper bound on each \(\eta_{a,k,v}\). Let \(b\) be any probability vector and \(\eta>0\). The zero-sum subspace
\[
 V_0=\{z\in\mathbb R^q:\mathbf 1^{\mathsf T}z=0\}
\]
is invariant under \(b\mathbf 1^{\mathsf T}+\eta Q_q\), and the restriction to \(V_0\) is \(\eta I_{V_0}\). Moreover
\[
 \mathbf 1^{\mathsf T}(b\mathbf 1^{\mathsf T}+\eta Q_q)
 =\mathbf 1^{\mathsf T},
\]
so the induced map on the one-dimensional quotient \(\mathbb R^q/V_0\) has eigenvalue \(1\). Therefore
\[
 \det(b\mathbf 1^{\mathsf T}+\eta Q_q)=1\cdot\eta^{q-1}.
\]
Consequently every corrected local table satisfies
\[
 d_{a,k,u}=\eta_{a,k,u_{A_{a,k}}}^{q-1}>0,
\]
and \(\Delta_{\mathrm{DT}}>0\) at this interior parameter point. Since its denominator is positive there, \(N_{\mathrm{DT}}\) is not identically zero.

For completeness, the measure and topology conclusion follows directly from polynomial algebra. A nonzero univariate polynomial has finitely many roots. Inducting on the number of affine coordinates and applying Fubini's theorem to the nonzero coefficient polynomials shows that the zero set of a nonzero multivariate polynomial has Lebesgue measure zero. The same induction shows that a polynomial vanishing on a nonempty relatively open box must be the zero polynomial; hence its zero set has empty relative interior. Applied to \(N_{\mathrm{DT}}\), these facts show that its complement in \(\Theta_{\Gamma,\Lambda}^{+}\) is relatively dense and has full measure. It is relatively open because \(\Delta_{\mathrm{DT}}\) is continuous where its denominators are positive, and it is nonempty by the displayed family.

The source lemma records the two-sufficient-measurement requirement of \(\mathcal M_{\mathrm{Chen}}\). In the present certified class, positive support and positive measurement tables imply
\[
 |\operatorname{supp}(H_k)|=q
 \quad\text{and}\quad
 |\operatorname{supp}(X_j)|=q
\]
for every \(k,j\). All measurements are discrete. Hence no observed variable in \(\mathcal M_{\mathrm{cert}}^{(q)}(K,J)\) is a sufficient measurement in the cited sense, because the required strict inequality \(q>q\) is false. Thus the two-sufficient-measurement condition fails for every member of the certified class.

This class is nonempty. On the graph \(\Gamma^{\star}\), the calculations in the proof attached to Proposition~\textnormal{prop:ternary-witness} establish strict positivity, measurement nondegeneracy, the graph conditions, and \(\Delta_{\mathrm{DT}}>0\) at \(P^{\star}\). These are finitely many strict polynomial or rational inequalities and persist in a relative neighborhood. Lemma~\textnormal{lem:positive-faithful-parameters-dense} supplies a faithful positive Markov parameter in that neighborhood. It is therefore a member of \(\mathcal M_{\mathrm{cert}}^{(3)}(3,8)\), but the equal-support calculation puts it outside \(\mathcal M_{\mathrm{Chen}}\). Hence \(\mathcal M_{\mathrm{cert}}^{(q)}(K,J)\) is not contained in \(\mathcal M_{\mathrm{Chen}}\) in the ambient universe in which both classes are compared.

Conversely, the cited definition expressly permits continuous sufficient measurements. For example, take one nondegenerate finite latent variable and three conditionally independent location-family continuous children with distinct latent-indexed locations and everywhere positive noise densities. The shifted densities are linearly independent, so the finite-state conditional expectation operator is complete; generic positive choices are faithful. This is a mixed-type member allowed by the cited class, but it cannot belong to \(\mathcal M_{\mathrm{cert}}^{(q)}(K,J)\), whose observed coordinates all have the finite state space \(\mathcal Q\). Thus the reverse containment fails already by support type. Independently, the multifactor graphs permitted by the cited class need not be double triangular: if two latent coordinates have only jointly parented observed children, then every such row contains both coordinates, so whichever coordinate is placed first in an order violates the required zero for the later coordinate. Finally, the cited discretization result explains the different rank mechanisms: completeness yields a discretization with a full-rank conditional table, whereas the present Theorems~\textnormal{thm:local-factorization} and~\textnormal{thm:certificate-frontier} derive full rank from the finite local determinants. This proves all asserted comparisons.

Let \(r=q^K\). Membership in the certified class, Assumption~\textnormal{ass:certificate}, and Theorem~\textnormal{thm:certificate-frontier} imply that \(M_1\) and \(M_2\) are invertible. Assumption~\textnormal{ass:positive-support} makes every diagonal entry of \(\operatorname{diag}(\pi)\) positive. Therefore
\[
 T_{12}=M_1\operatorname{diag}(\pi)M_2^{\mathsf T}
\]
is a product of three invertible \(r\times r\) matrices, and
\[
 \operatorname{rank}(T_{12})=r=q^K.
\]

Now consider any \(q\)-state measurement-model realization of the same observed law with \(L\) latent coordinates. Conditional independence of observed vertices given the complete latent vector gives a factorization of the same two-view matrix as
\[
 T_{12}=\widetilde M_1\operatorname{diag}(\widetilde\pi)
 \widetilde M_2^{\mathsf T},
\]
where each \(\widetilde M_a\) has \(q^L\) columns. Hence
\[
 q^K=\operatorname{rank}(T_{12})\le q^L.
\]
Because \(q\ge3>1\), this inequality implies \(L\ge K\). The original realization shows \(K_{\min}(P_X)\le K\), while the rank argument gives \(K_{\min}(P_X)\ge K\). Thus \(K_{\min}(P_X)=K\). The competing realization was used only through its measurement-model factorization, so no triangularity or certificate was imposed on it.

For each observed coordinate \(j\), let
\[
 A_j=\{k:H_k\to X_j\text{ in }G\}\subseteq\{1,\ldots,K\}.
\]
Given anonymous component labels corresponding to latent configurations \(h,h'\in\mathcal Q^K\), the measurement Markov property implies that \(h_{A_j}=h'_{A_j}\) gives equal conditional columns for \(X_j\). Assumption~\textnormal{ass:measurement-nondegeneracy} gives the converse. Thus the observable relation \(E_j\) is, after any one unknown labeling of the components,
\[
 E_j=E_{A_j},\qquad
 h\mathrel{E_A}h'\quad\Longleftrightarrow\quad h_A=h'_A.
\]

The coordinate product is recoverable from the finite lattice generated by these relations. For subsets \(A,B\subseteq\{1,\ldots,K\}\), direct inspection gives
\[
 E_A\wedge E_B=E_{A\cup B},\qquad E_A\vee E_B=E_{A\cap B}.
\]
For the second identity, if \(h\) and \(h'\) agree on \(A\cap B\), choose \(z\) with \(z_A=h_A\) and \(z_B=h'_B\), which is consistent on the intersection; then \(h\mathrel{E_A}z\mathrel{E_B}h'\). The reverse inclusion is immediate. Hence every element of the generated relation lattice is \(E_A\) for a set \(A\) in the set lattice generated by the \(A_j\)'s, and \(E_A\) has exactly \(q^{|A|}\) equivalence classes.

Write \(C_k=\{j:k\in A_j\}=\operatorname{ch}_X(H_k)\). Assumption~\textnormal{ass:subset} says that for every \(\ell\ne k\), \(C_k\not\subseteq C_\ell\). Therefore some \(j\in C_k\setminus C_\ell\), and consequently
\[
 \bigcap_{j\in C_k}A_j=\{k\}.
\]
The family \(C_k\) is nonempty by third-view coverage. Using the join identity, \(E_{\{k\}}=\bigvee_{j\in C_k}E_j\) belongs to the observable generated lattice. Conversely, an element \(E_A\) of that lattice has exactly \(q\) classes if and only if \(|A|=1\). Thus the \(K\) one-coordinate relations \(E_{\{1\}},\ldots,E_{\{K\}}\) are characterized observably as all lattice elements having exactly \(q\) classes.

Permuting these \(K\) relations and naming the \(q\) classes of each relation are precisely the actions of \(\mathfrak S_K\) and \((\mathfrak S_q)^K\). After such choices, the map
\[
 \varphi_{\mathrm{coord}}(\ell)
 =\bigl([\ell]_{E_{\{1\}}},\ldots,[\ell]_{E_{\{K\}}}\bigr)
\]
is injective because the meet of all \(E_{\{k\}}\) is equality. Its domain and codomain both have \(q^K\) elements, so it is bijective. This proves uniqueness modulo \(\mathfrak G\).

The parent set of \(X_j\) is then recovered by
\[
 k\in A_j\quad\Longleftrightarrow\quad E_j\subseteq E_{\{k\}},
\]
so \(\Gamma\) is identified. Transporting the already recovered component weights and columns through \(\varphi_{\mathrm{coord}}\) gives \(\pi\) and every table \(p_j(\cdot\mid h_{A_j})\). Finally, the recovered \(\pi\) determines every latent conditional-independence statement by finite marginalization. Observed vertices are sinks, so d-separation statements involving only latent vertices and latent conditioning sets are the same in \(G\) and in its latent subgraph \(\Lambda\). Assumption~\textnormal{ass:faithfulness} therefore makes the recovered latent conditional-independence pattern equal to the d-separation pattern of \(\Lambda\). The skeleton is recovered by declaring two latent vertices adjacent exactly when no conditioning subset separates them; an unshielded triple is a collider exactly when its middle vertex is absent from every separating set of its endpoints. DAGs have the same d-separation pattern exactly when these recovered skeletons and unshielded colliders agree, so the Markov equivalence class \([\Lambda]_{\mathrm{MEC}}\) is identified. This completes the claimed alignment step.

Set \(r=q^K\), and regard the joint observed law on the three disjoint views as a three-way tensor. For \(z\in\mathcal Q^{|S_3|}\), let \(T_z\) be its \(r\times r\) slice at \(X_{S_3}=z\), and let \(m_3(z\mid h)=P(X_{S_3}=z\mid H=h)\). Conditional independence of observed variables given \(H\) gives
\[
 T_z=M_1\operatorname{diag}\bigl(\pi_hm_3(z\mid h):h\in\mathcal Q^K\bigr)M_2^{\mathsf T}.
\]
Theorem~\textnormal{thm:certificate-frontier} makes \(M_1,M_2\) invertible, and positive support makes \(\operatorname{diag}(\pi)\) invertible. Therefore \(T_{12}=\sum_zT_z\) is invertible and
\[
 C_z:=T_zT_{12}^{-1}
 =M_1\operatorname{diag}\bigl(m_3(z\mid h):h\in\mathcal Q^K\bigr)M_1^{-1}.
\]

The third-view component columns are pairwise distinct. Indeed, if \(h\ne h'\), choose \(k\) with \(h_k\ne h'_k\). Third-view coverage provides \(j\in S_3\) with \(k\in A_j\); the two parent configurations at \(j\) differ, so measurement nondegeneracy makes the conditional marginal columns for \(X_j\), and hence the joint columns \(m_3(\cdot\mid h)\) and \(m_3(\cdot\mid h')\), distinct.

There is consequently a real vector \(t=(t_z)_z\) for which all numbers
\[
 \lambda_h=\sum_z t_zm_3(z\mid h)
\]
are distinct: the excluded choices are the finite union of proper hyperplanes \(t\cdot(m_3(\cdot\mid h)-m_3(\cdot\mid h'))=0\). The observable matrix \(C(t)=\sum_zt_zC_z\) has simple spectrum and eigenvectors equal to the columns of \(M_1\), up to one common permutation and nonzero column scalings. Normalizing each eigenvector to have entries summing to one removes the scalings because each true column is a probability vector. Then
\[
 W=M_1^{-1}T_{12}=\operatorname{diag}(\pi)M_2^{\mathsf T},
 \qquad
 \pi_h=\sum_{x_2}W(h,x_2),
 \qquad
 M_2^{\mathsf T}=\operatorname{diag}(\pi)^{-1}W,
\]
where division is valid by positive support. Finally \(M_1^{-1}C_zM_1\) recovers every \(m_3(z\mid h)\). Marginalizing the recovered joint-view columns recovers the conditional column of every individual observed variable. Thus \(P_X\) determines the component labels, weights, and all measurement columns up to one arbitrary permutation of the \(r\) labels.

Theorem~\textnormal{thm:coordinate-alignment} now transforms those anonymous labels into the unique \(K\)-coordinate product modulo \(\mathfrak G\), recovers \(\Gamma,\pi,p\), and recovers \([\Lambda]_{\mathrm{MEC}}\) from faithfulness. This proves that \(P_X\) determines \(\mathcal R(P_X)\).

It remains to justify the comparison-domain assertion. Any element of \(\mathcal C_K(P_X)\) supplies another \(r\)-term product decomposition of the same three-view tensor with all \(r\) weights positive. Since \(T_{12}\) has rank \(r\), both alternative first- and second-view factor matrices must have rank \(r\). Applying that alternative decomposition to the observable simple-spectrum matrix \(C(t)\) shows that its first-view columns are the same eigenvectors, up to the same permutation and probability normalization. The displayed formulas then force the same weights, second-view columns, and third-view columns. Its measurement nondegeneracy and subset condition imply, by the lattice proof of Theorem~\textnormal{thm:coordinate-alignment}, the same coordinate factors and \(\Gamma\) modulo \(\mathfrak G\). Its faithfulness gives the same latent Markov equivalence class. Hence every comparison-domain realization lies in the same \(\sim\)-class, as claimed.

Each row of \(\Gamma^{\star}\) has the claimed triangular pattern: rows \(1,2,3\) have diagonal parents \(1,2,3\) in order \((1,2,3)\), and rows \(4,5,6\) have diagonal parents \(2,1,3\) in order \((2,1,3)\), with no later parent in either case. Rows \(7,8\) cover all three latent coordinates. The observed-child sets are
\[
 \{1,2,3,5,6,7\},\qquad
 \{2,3,4,5,6,8\},\qquad
 \{3,6,7,8\}.
\]
Each ordered pair has an element in the first set but not the second, so none contains another. Every child \(3,6,7,8\) of the third latent coordinate has at least two latent parents, proving the no-pure-child assertion.

For a fixed row \(j\), normalization follows from
\[
 \sum_{x=0}^{2}\left(\mathbf1\{x=h_\ell\}-\frac13\right)=0.
\]
Moreover
\[
 \sum_{\ell:\Gamma^{\star}_{j\ell}=1}c^{\star}_{j\ell}
 \le 2^{-(4+j)}\sum_{\ell=1}^{3}8^{-\ell}<\frac1{224}.
\]
Thus every conditional probability lies strictly between
\[
 \frac13-\frac1{3\cdot224}>0
 \quad\text{and}\quad
 \frac13+\frac2{3\cdot224}<1.
\]
Uniform independent latent coordinates and conditional independence of observed coordinates therefore define a strictly positive law Markov to the stated graph.

Measurement nondegeneracy also follows from the geometric coefficients. If two parent configurations differ, let \(\ell_0\) be the smallest differing parent index. At \(x=h_{\ell_0}\), the contribution of that parent to the difference of the two conditional probabilities has absolute value \(c^{\star}_{j\ell_0}\), while all later-parent contributions together have absolute value at most
\[
 \sum_{\ell>\ell_0}c^{\star}_{j\ell}<c^{\star}_{j\ell_0}.
\]
The difference is therefore nonzero.

Independence of the latent coordinates makes conditioning on a predecessor context leave later latent states uniform and does not alter the displayed measurement table. For each selected row, separation of the diagonal-parent term gives exactly
\[
 B_{a,k,u}=b^{\star}_{s(a,k),u}\mathbf1^{\mathsf T}
 +c^{\star}_{s(a,k),\rho_a(k)}Q_3.
\]
The invariant-subspace determinant calculation in Theorem~\textnormal{thm:certificate-genericity}, with \(q=3\), yields
\[
 \det(B_{a,k,u})=
 \bigl(c^{\star}_{s(a,k),\rho_a(k)}\bigr)^2>0.
\]
Hence \(\Delta_{\mathrm{DT}}>0\). Strict positivity, finitely many column inequalities, and finitely many nonzero determinants persist in a relative neighborhood of the table parameter. Lemma~\textnormal{lem:positive-faithful-parameters-dense} shows that faithful parameters form a dense full-measure subset of this neighborhood; because rational points are dense and a finite union of proper polynomial zero sets cannot contain an open rational box, a rational faithful point may be chosen there. It satisfies every defining property of \(\mathcal M_{\mathrm{cert}}^{(3)}(3,8)\). Theorem~\textnormal{thm:fixed-k-identification} then identifies its recovery target. This proves the narrowed statement while making no unsupported assertion that the particular displayed coefficients are faithful.

theorem.statement: There is a finite exact-real-arithmetic algorithm \(A_q\), obtained by making every enumeration and query in \(\mathsf H_q\) explicit, which halts for every probability mass function \(P_X\). On every \(P_X\) generated by \(\mathcal M_{\mathrm{cert}}^{(q)}(K,J)\), it recovers \(K\), retains only exact realizations of \(P_X\), represents every member of \(\mathcal C_K(P_X)\), and returns exactly \(\mathcal R(P_X)\). Its recursive classification stage terminates under the lexicographic measure consisting of the number of unclassified observed rows followed by the number of unresolved component pairs.
theorem.proof_tex:
All operations below are over exact real numbers; equality, rank, polynomial coefficients, and eigenvalues are therefore queried without a numerical tolerance.

First determine the latent dimension. For every integer \(L\) with \(2L+1\le J\), enumerate the finitely many ordered pairs of disjoint \(L\)-row sets \(R_1,R_2\), form the observable \(q^L\times q^L\) matrix
\[
 U_{R_1,R_2}(x_1,x_2)=P_X(X_{R_1}=x_1,X_{R_2}=x_2),
\]
and query its determinant. Define \(\widehat K\) as the largest \(L\) for which one such determinant is nonzero, returning a failure symbol if no such \(L\) exists. On a certified input, \(L=K\) is feasible by Theorem~\textnormal{thm:latent-dimension}. Every observable unfolding under the true \(q^K\)-component mixture has rank at most \(q^K\), so a square \(q^L\times q^L\) unfolding cannot be invertible when \(L>K\). Hence \(\widehat K=K\).

Now enumerate every ordered pair of disjoint \(K\)-row views and use the nonempty complement as a third view. Discard a pair if its two-view matrix \(T_{12}\) is singular. For a retained pair form all slices \(T_z\) and matrices \(C_z=T_zT_{12}^{-1}\). Let
\[
 g(t)=\operatorname{disc}\!\left(\sum_z t_zC_z\right),
\]
the discriminant of its characteristic polynomial. This is an observable polynomial of finite degree. Determine its coefficients exactly. If it is zero, discard the branch. If it is nonzero, a finite Cartesian grid with more points per coordinate than the degree of \(g\) contains a point \(t\) with \(g(t)\ne0\); exhaustive evaluation finds one and terminates. Diagonalize the resulting simple-spectrum matrix, normalize eigenvectors to have column sum one, and use
\[
 W=M_1^{-1}T_{12},\qquad
 \pi_h=\sum_{x_2}W(h,x_2),\qquad
 M_2^{\mathsf T}=\operatorname{diag}(\pi)^{-1}W,
 \qquad
 m_3(z\mid h)=\bigl(M_1^{-1}C_zM_1\bigr)_{hh}
\]
to reconstruct the branch. Reject it unless all quantities are real, strictly positive probability tables and their tensor product reproduces every cell of \(P_X\). The proof of Theorem~\textnormal{thm:fixed-k-identification} shows that the true views pass these tests: their third-view columns are distinct, so their discriminant polynomial is nonzero, and the formulas recover their unique \(q^K\)-component decomposition up to label permutation.

For each surviving decomposition, marginalize its three view columns to obtain every component-conditional column of every \(X_j\). Reject a branch unless, component by component, the product of those individual columns equals each recovered joint-view column. Query all equalities defining \(E_j\), close the finite family under meet and join, and select the relations with exactly \(q\) classes. Retain a branch only if there are exactly \(K\) such coordinate relations, their common meet is equality, and their class map is a bijection onto a product of \(K\) \(q\)-element sets. Theorem~\textnormal{thm:coordinate-alignment} proves that the true branch passes and that these relations are unique modulo \(\mathfrak G\). For each row, recover its parent set by the refinement tests \(E_j\subseteq E_{\{k\}}\), reconstruct \(\Gamma,\pi,p\), and evaluate every local minor \(d_{a,k,u}\) as a recorded certificate and pruning trace.

Finally enumerate the finite set of DAGs on the \(K\) recovered latent coordinates. From the recovered positive \(\pi\), compute every latent conditional-independence cross-product exactly and retain only DAGs over which \(\pi\) factorizes. For each resulting complete graph and reconstructed complete-data law, enumerate all conditional-independence cross-products on \(H,X\) and compare them with all d-separation statements; retain the graph only when full faithfulness holds. Also check measurement nondegeneracy, the subset condition, positivity, and the exact marginal identity with \(P_X\). Thus every retained object is an actual member of \(\mathcal C_K(P_X)\), establishing soundness. Conversely, any member of \(\mathcal C_K(P_X)\) gives an \(r=q^K\)-term decomposition of the same tensor. The simple-spectrum argument in Theorem~\textnormal{thm:fixed-k-identification} forces that decomposition, its equality lattice, and its latent conditional-independence pattern to occur in the enumerated lists. It is therefore represented, establishing completeness. All retained objects have the single quotient value \(\mathcal R(P_X)\), again by that theorem, so this is the output of \(A_q\).

Every outer set being enumerated is finite. The grid search is finite by the degree bound, lattice closure is finite because the label set is finite, and the DAG list is finite. To match the stated recursive handle, assign a branch the pair
\[
 \mu=(u,v),
\]
where \(u\) is the number of observed rows whose equality pattern has not yet been classified and \(v\) is the number of component pairs not yet resolved by the queried relations. A row-classification transition decreases \(u\); once \(u=0\), a pair-resolution transition decreases \(v\); pruning halts the branch. Lexicographic order on \(\mathbb N^2\) is well founded, so no recursive branch is infinite. Together with the finite outer enumerations, this proves termination on every exact \(P_X\) and completes the construction.

added_lemmas.statement: For any fixed directed acyclic graph \(G\) on finitely many \(q\)-state vertices, the table parameters in the strictly positive Markov parameterization whose induced law \(P\) is faithful to \(G\) form a relatively open dense set of full Lebesgue measure in the affine product of conditional-table simplex interiors.
added_lemmas.proof_tex:
There are only finitely many triples \((V,W,C)\), where \(V\) and \(W\) are distinct vertices and \(C\) is a set of other vertices. In a strictly positive finite law, \(V\mathrel{\perp}W\mid C\) is equivalent to the finite collection of cross-product equations
\[
 P(v,w,c)P(v',w',c)-P(v,w',c)P(v',w,c)=0
\]
for all states \(v,v',w,w',c\). Under the Markov table parameterization every left-hand side is a polynomial in the free conditional-table entries.

Suppose \(V\) and \(W\) are d-connected given \(C\). Choose an active trail. To see that the corresponding collection of polynomials is not identically zero, first work at the closure of the binary submodel. Along each noncollider segment, let every vertex copy the preceding binary bit. At every collider, let its binary value be the exclusive-or of the two incident trail bits; if the collider itself is not in \(C\), copy that value along a directed path to the descendant in \(C\) whose existence makes the trail active. Set vertices and arrows not used by this construction to independent constants. Conditioning the indicated collider or descendant values to be zero imposes successive parity equalities along the trail, so the two endpoint bits have a nonzero \(2\times2\) cross-product minor. No noncollider on the active trail lies in \(C\), so no copying segment is blocked. For \(q>2\), embed the two binary states into \(\mathcal Q\). This boundary construction factorizes over \(G\) and makes at least one displayed polynomial nonzero. A sufficiently small perturbation of all deterministic conditional tables gives strictly positive \(q\)-state tables while preserving that strict nonzero inequality. Thus, for every d-connected triple, at least one of its conditional-independence polynomials is a nonzero polynomial on the Markov parameter space.

An unfaithful Markov parameter lies in the finite union, over d-connected triples, of the common zero sets just described; selecting one nonzero polynomial per triple puts this union inside a finite union of nonzero polynomial zero sets. The elementary polynomial argument used in the proof of Theorem~\textnormal{thm:certificate-genericity} gives measure zero and empty relative interior. Its complement is therefore dense and full measure. It is relatively open because it is a finite intersection of strict polynomial inequalities. This proves the claim without assuming faithfulness at a particular numerical parameter point.

added_lemmas.statement: In the mixed latent-structure class \(\mathcal M_{\mathrm{Chen}}\), every latent-parent set is required to have two sufficient measured variables; a sufficient measured variable is either continuous or, if discrete, has support cardinality strictly larger than that of its latent parent. The class permits continuous measurements and multifactor observed variables with several latent parents, and it does not impose two disjoint triangular views. Under the stated completeness condition, a continuous measurement admits a discretization whose conditional table has full rank, and the resulting mixed latent structure is identified up to a latent Markov equivalence class under the additional conditions of their identification theorem.

proposed_definition_changes.proposed:
Set the latent coordinates independent and uniform. For a selected row \(j=s(a,k)\), let \(A_{a,k}=\operatorname{pa}_{\Gamma}(j)\cap\{\rho_a(1),\ldots,\rho_a(k-1)\}\). For each \(v\in\mathcal Q^{A_{a,k}}\), choose a strictly positive probability vector \(b_{a,k,v}\) and a number \(\eta_{a,k,v}>0\), small enough that all entries below are positive, and define the compatible measurement table by
\[
 P(X_j=x\mid H_{\operatorname{pa}_{\Gamma}(j)}=h)
 =b_{a,k,h_{A_{a,k}}}(x)
 +\eta_{a,k,h_{A_{a,k}}}\bigl(\mathbf 1\{x=h_{\rho_a(k)}\}-q^{-1}\bigr).
\]
Equivalently, the induced local matrix is \(B_{a,k,u}=b_{a,k,u_{A_{a,k}}}\mathbf 1^{\mathsf T}+\eta_{a,k,u_{A_{a,k}}}Q_q\); thus both \(b\) and \(\eta\) are constant when only nonparent coordinates of \(u\) change. Assign arbitrary strictly positive graph-compatible tables to unselected observed rows.
proposed_definition_changes.reason: The frozen construction allows its base vector and amplitude to vary with predecessor coordinates that are not parents of the selected observed row. Such variation is not compatible with the fixed measurement graph. The corrected formula indexes both objects only by the actual predecessor-parent subconfiguration and removes the determinant assertion from the construction; the proof derives that determinant.

proposed_assumptions.condition: The observations \(X_1,\ldots,X_n\) are independent and identically distributed with common probability mass function \(P_X\) on the fixed finite space \(\mathcal Q^J\).
proposed_assumptions.reason: A familywise type-I error or power probability for the empirical mass function is undefined until the joint sampling law is specified. Independent sampling from the observed law is the standard condition needed for the multinomial concentration and bootstrap argument.
proposed_assumptions.not_crux: This assumption specifies only the sampling mechanism. It does not assert bootstrap validity, multiplicity control, power, separation, or any population identification conclusion.

proposed.statement: The proposed equal-alphabet certified class and \(\mathcal M_{\mathrm{Chen}}\) are incomparable in the ambient mixed-type latent-structure universe. On \(\mathcal M_{\mathrm{cert}}^{(q)}(K,J)\), every selected observed variable has support \(q\), so Chen et al.'s discrete sufficient-measurement requirement \( |\operatorname{supp}(X_j)|>|\operatorname{supp}(H_k)|\) fails when both supports equal \(q\); the dense ternary witness is therefore outside their two-sufficient-measurement class. Conversely, \(\mathcal M_{\mathrm{Chen}}\) permits continuous measurements and graphs without two disjoint triangular views, so it is not contained in \(\mathcal M_{\mathrm{cert}}^{(q)}(K,J)\). Completeness in Chen et al. supplies a discretization with full-rank tables, whereas this project derives full rank from the finite local certificate without assuming completeness or larger-support measurements.
proposed.justification: The class relation prevents the new certificate from being presented as a disguised instance of completeness or two sufficient measurements.
proposed.gap: Chen et al. (2025, Proposition 4.2, Definition 4.1, and Theorem 4.19) cover mixed-type measurements through completeness and two sufficient measurements, not equal-state double-triangular tables.
proposed.consumer: It tells practitioners whether a mixed-type tensor-rank guarantee or the local categorical certificate applies to a given item bank.

proposed.statement: Suppose \((G,P)\in\mathcal M_{\mathrm{cert}}^{(q)}(K,J)\) and a three-view decomposition has recovered \(\mathscr L(P_X)\) and the component conditional columns up to one arbitrary permutation. The observable family \(\mathcal E(P_X)\), together with measurement nondegeneracy and the subset condition, determines a bijection \(\varphi_{\mathrm{coord}}:\mathscr L(P_X)\to\mathcal Q^K\) uniquely modulo \(\mathfrak G\). Transporting the recovered weights and conditional columns through this bijection identifies \(\Gamma,\pi,p\); faithfulness then identifies \([\Lambda]_{\mathrm{MEC}}\). Thus the passage from \(q^K\) anonymous mixture labels to \(K\) \(q\)-state coordinates and a latent MEC is an additional identification step not supplied by generic three-view Kruskal uniqueness.
proposed.justification: Anonymous latent-class labels are insufficient for a causal measurement graph; the equality-pattern theorem supplies the missing coordinate product and MEC.
proposed.gap: Allman, Matias, and Rhodes (2009) stop at label swapping for one latent-class variable, while Kivva et al. (2021) obtain coordinate structure from a supplied mixture oracle.
proposed.consumer: It lets an identifiability checker report named latent coordinates, their observed-child sets, and a latent MEC.

proposed.statement: For every \((G,P)\in\mathcal M_{\mathrm{cert}}^{(q)}(K,J)\), the observed law \(P_X\) first determines only the unstructured \(q^K\)-label set \(\mathscr L(P_X)\) through generic three-view uniqueness; the component-equality pattern \(\mathcal E(P_X)\) then uniquely aligns those labels with \(K\) \(q\)-state coordinates through \(\varphi_{\mathrm{coord}}\), modulo \(\mathfrak G\), and latent conditional independences determine \([\Lambda]_{\mathrm{MEC}}\). Consequently \(P_X\) uniquely determines \(\mathcal R(P_X)=[\Gamma,\pi,p,[\Lambda]_{\mathrm{MEC}}]_{\sim}\); equivalently, every realization in the fully enumerated domain \(\mathcal C_K(P_X)\) belongs to the same \(\sim\)-equivalence class.

proposed.gap: Existing latent-class uniqueness results do not by themselves recover the coordinate product, measurement adjacency, or latent MEC.
proposed.consumer: It certifies that a recovered polytomous skill graph and latent MEC are not artifacts of another same-dimension realization.

open_obligations.what_is_open: Derive a multiplicity-calibrated familywise type-I error bound and uniform separated power statement for the adaptive empirical query family after a sampling law has been added.
open_obligations.obstruction: The frozen core specifies the formula for the empirical mass function but no probability law for the observations. For example, the observations could all repeat one arbitrary draw, in which case the empirical law need not converge to the observed law. Thus neither a type-I error probability nor bootstrap validity follows from the frozen primitives.
open_obligations.attempted: Reduced every raw rank query to a finite-dimensional perturbation bound and every reconstructed minor, away from singular intersections, to a continuous rational functional. This closes deterministic stability but cannot create stochastic convergence or calibration.
open_obligations.partial_result: For the finite population query family, every raw unfolding is a linear map of \(P_X\), so there is a finite constant \(C(q,K,J)\) such that \(\|\widehat U-U\|_{\mathrm{op}}\le C(q,K,J)\|\widehat P_n-P_X\|_{\infty}\). The variational characterization \(\sigma_{\min}(U)=\min_{\|v\|_2=1}\|Uv\|_2\) and the triangle inequality then give \(|\sigma_{\min}(\widehat U)-\sigma_{\min}(U)|\le C(q,K,J)\|\widehat P_n-P_X\|_{\infty}\). On a branch with simple spectrum and positive conditioning denominators, reconstructed local minors are continuous rational functions of \(P_X\). Consequently any deterministic sequence with \(\|\widehat P_n-P_X\|_{\infty}\to0\) eventually makes all decisions correctly whenever the stated \(\kappa\)-separation holds. A familywise probability guarantee, however, requires a sampling law and cannot be deduced from this deterministic statement.

proofs.proof_tex:
We prove the proposed, source-faithful version of the proposition.  Fix
\((G_{\mathrm{bin}},P_{\mathrm{bin}})\in
\mathcal M_{\mathrm{LG},1}^{\mathrm{bin}}(K,J)\).  By the definition of this
class, the binary measurement-graph, Markov, positive-latent-support,
measurement-nondegeneracy, and double-triangular conditions hold.  The binary
triangular-view lemma below, applied once to each of the two disjoint ordered
views, gives
\[
 \operatorname{rank}((M_{\mathrm{bin}})_a)=2^K,
 \qquad a\in\{1,2\}.
\]
Each matrix is square of order \(2^K\), so both matrices are nonsingular.  This
step uses the measurement-graph, Markov, nondegeneracy, and
double-triangular assumptions; in particular, it does not use faithfulness.

By positive latent support,
\((\pi_{\mathrm{bin}})_h>0\) for every
\(h\in\mathcal Q_{\mathrm{bin}}^K\).  Hence
\(D:=\operatorname{diag}(\pi_{\mathrm{bin}})\) is nonsingular.  The observable
factorization in the definition of \((T_{12})_{\mathrm{bin}}\) therefore yields
\[
 (T_{12})_{\mathrm{bin}}
 = (M_{\mathrm{bin}})_1D(M_{\mathrm{bin}})_2^{\mathsf T},
 \qquad
 (T_{12})_{\mathrm{bin}}^{-1}
 = (M_{\mathrm{bin}})_2^{-\mathsf T}D^{-1}
   (M_{\mathrm{bin}})_1^{-1}.
\]
Thus
\[
 \operatorname{rank}((T_{12})_{\mathrm{bin}})=2^K.
\]

We next distinguish the observed-law functional
\((K_{\min})_{\mathrm{bin}}\) from the true latent dimension and prove their
equality.  The displayed member of
\(\mathcal M_{\mathrm{LG},1}^{\mathrm{bin}}(K,J)\) is a binary
measurement-model realization with \(K\) latent coordinates, so the defining
minimum gives
\[
 (K_{\min})_{\mathrm{bin}}((P_X)_{\mathrm{bin}})\leq K.
\]
Conversely, suppose the same observed law had a binary measurement-model
realization with \(L<K\) latent coordinates.  Let \(\widetilde H\in
\mathcal Q_{\mathrm{bin}}^L\) be its latent vector, let
\(\widetilde\pi\) be its latent mass vector, and let
\(\widetilde M_a\) be the conditional table of the \(K\) observed variables
in view \((S_a)_{\mathrm{bin}}\) given \(\widetilde H\).  The
measurement-graph and Markov properties of a measurement-model realization
give conditional independence of the observed vertices given all latent
vertices.  Therefore the same observable two-view matrix factors as
\[
 (T_{12})_{\mathrm{bin}}
 =\widetilde M_1\operatorname{diag}(\widetilde\pi)
   \widetilde M_2^{\mathsf T},
 \qquad
 \widetilde M_a\in\mathbb R^{2^K\times 2^L}.
\]
The elementary rank inequality for a matrix product, obtained because the
image of a product is contained in the image of its first factor, gives
\[
 \operatorname{rank}((T_{12})_{\mathrm{bin}})
 \leq 2^L<2^K,
\]
contradicting the established rank \(2^K\).  Hence every realization in the
defining minimum has \(L\geq K\), and the two inequalities prove
\[
 (K_{\min})_{\mathrm{bin}}((P_X)_{\mathrm{bin}})=K.
\]
The cited Lee--Gu Theorem 1 record states the corresponding published binary
rank argument and latent-dimension conclusion.  Our derivation shows directly
that its rank argument remains valid on the frozen comparator class without
using faithfulness; it does not assert that this reduced list is identical to
all of Lee and Gu's standing BLCM assumptions.

Now fix
\((G_{\mathrm{bin}},P_{\mathrm{bin}})\in
\mathcal M_{\mathrm{LG},2}^{\mathrm{bin}}(K,J)\).  By the definition of this
class it is also in \(\mathcal M_{\mathrm{LG},1}^{\mathrm{bin}}(K,J)\), so the
preceding equality identifies \(K\) from the observed law.  The additional
third-view condition is exactly
\[
 \forall k\in\{1,\ldots,K\}\quad
 \exists j\in(S_3)_{\mathrm{bin}}
 \quad (\Gamma_{\mathrm{bin}})_{jk}=1,
\]
which says that every column of the residual block \(\Gamma_3\) is nonempty.
The class also imposes faithfulness and the subset condition, while membership
in the first class supplies the remaining standing BLCM and
double-triangular conditions.  Thus every hypothesis of the cited Lee--Gu
Theorem 2 record is satisfied.  That theorem identifies
\(\Gamma_{\mathrm{bin}}\), the complete binary law \(P_{\mathrm{bin}}\), and
the latent graph \(\Lambda_{\mathrm{bin}}\) up to coordinate permutation,
binary state flips, and latent Markov equivalence.

Finally, the identified complete law determines
\[
 (\pi_{\mathrm{bin}})_h=P_{\mathrm{bin}}(H_{\mathrm{bin}}=h)
 \quad\text{and}\quad
 (p_{\mathrm{bin}})_j(x\mid h)
 =\frac{P_{\mathrm{bin}}((X_{\mathrm{bin}})_j=x,
                         H_{\mathrm{bin}}=h)}
        {(\pi_{\mathrm{bin}})_h}.
\]
The division is valid by positive latent support.  Coordinate permutations
and binary state flips form
\(\mathfrak G_{\mathrm{bin}}=\mathfrak S_K\ltimes(\mathfrak S_2)^K\), and
the remaining graphical ambiguity is exactly the latent MEC.  Consequently
the observed law uniquely determines
\[
 \mathcal R_{\mathrm{bin}}((P_X)_{\mathrm{bin}})
 = [\Gamma_{\mathrm{bin}},\pi_{\mathrm{bin}},p_{\mathrm{bin}},
      [\Lambda_{\mathrm{bin}}]_{\mathrm{MEC}}]
   \quad\text{modulo }\mathfrak G_{\mathrm{bin}},
\]
which proves the second assertion.

added_lemmas.statement:
For every
\((G_{\mathrm{bin}},P_{\mathrm{bin}})\in
\mathcal M_{\mathrm{LG},1}^{\mathrm{bin}}(K,J)\) and every
\(a\in\{1,2\}\), the square conditional table
\((M_{\mathrm{bin}})_a\) is nonsingular.  This conclusion requires the
binary measurement-graph, Markov, measurement-nondegeneracy, and
double-triangular conditions, but neither faithfulness nor positive latent
support.
added_lemmas.proof_tex:
Fix a view \(a\).  Permute its selected observed coordinates and the latent
coordinates according to \((\rho_{\mathrm{bin}})_a\); row and column
permutations preserve nonsingularity.  In this order the selected row at stage
\(t\) has \(H_t\) as a parent and has no latent parent among
\(H_{t+1},\ldots,H_K\), by binary double triangularity.  By the measurement
graph and Markov factorization, conditional on all latent variables the
selected observed variables are independent, and the conditional law of the
stage-\(t\) observation depends only on latent parents among
\(H_1,\ldots,H_t\).

For \(t=0,1,\ldots,K\), let \(A_t\) be the \(2^t\times2^t\) conditional
table of the first \(t\) selected observed coordinates given
\((H_1,\ldots,H_t)\), with \(A_0=(1)\).  Suppose inductively that
\(A_{t-1}\) is nonsingular.  For every
\(u\in\{0,1\}^{t-1}\), define the \(2\times2\) table
\[
 C_u(x,r)=P_{\mathrm{bin}}
 \bigl((X_{\mathrm{bin}})_{s_{\mathrm{bin}}(a,t)}=x
       \mid H_{1:t-1}=u,H_t=r\bigr),
 \qquad x,r\in\{0,1\}.
\]
The diagonal one in the triangular row says that \(H_t\) is a parent of this
observation.  Binary measurement nondegeneracy therefore makes the two
conditional Bernoulli laws indexed by \(r=0\) and \(r=1\) distinct.  If
\(\theta_{u,r}:=P_{\mathrm{bin}}((X_{\mathrm{bin}})_{s_{\mathrm{bin}}(a,t)}=1
\mid H_{1:t-1}=u,H_t=r)\), then
\[
 C_u=
 \begin{pmatrix}
 1-\theta_{u,0}&1-\theta_{u,1}\\
 \theta_{u,0}&\theta_{u,1}
 \end{pmatrix},
 \qquad
 \det(C_u)=\theta_{u,1}-\theta_{u,0}\neq0.
\]
Thus every \(C_u\) is nonsingular; no entrywise positivity is needed.

Indexing rows by \((z,x)\) and columns by \((u,r)\), conditional independence
gives the entrywise identity
\[
 A_t((z,x),(u,r))=A_{t-1}(z,u)C_u(x,r).
\]
Equivalently, after the indicated lexicographic ordering,
\[
 A_t=(A_{t-1}\otimes I_2)
     \operatorname{blockdiag}_{u\in\{0,1\}^{t-1}}(C_u).
\]
The first factor is invertible with inverse
\(A_{t-1}^{-1}\otimes I_2\), and the second is invertible with blockwise
inverse \(\operatorname{blockdiag}_u(C_u^{-1})\).  Hence \(A_t\) is
nonsingular.  Induction from \(A_0=(1)\) proves that \(A_K\) is nonsingular.
After undoing the initial permutations, \(A_K=(M_{\mathrm{bin}})_a\).  Since
\(a\) was arbitrary, the result holds for both views.

added_lemmas.statement:
In the binary-response specialization of Lee and Gu (2026), double
triangularity under their standing BLCM conditions makes both triangular-view
conditional tables and their observable two-view probability matrix have rank
\(2^K\), and it identifies \(K\) against alternative BLCMs with fewer than
\(K\) binary latent coordinates.
